mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5.5% for two consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.5 and UNRATE declines for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a supply-side downturn, which raises input costs and reduces output, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-mo moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in the same month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises AND PAYEMS falls by >100,000 in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) over three months indicates a disinflationary tightening, which initially depresses growth but ultimately supports real interest rates and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-mo moving average for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month average for three consecutive months, combined with a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which typically precedes a consumer demand slowdown and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo average for 3 consecutive months AND GDPC1 declines
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
